docs.title: terranode
docs.text: terranode helps organizations configure GIS field projects, send field teams out with a mobile app to collect data — points, lines, polygons, photos, video, and audio — and bring that data back into a shared map, even when the field has no signal.

docs.title: What you can do today
docs.text:
• Catalog management — import base maps, vector layers, and raster layers once, then reuse them across as many projects as you need.
  • Project management — define a project's boundary, choose which catalog layers and surveys apply, and track progress from a dashboard.
  • Survey collection — build custom forms field users fill out on mobile, with full support for offline capture and later sync.
  • Organization-based access — every user belongs to one organization; project owners configure projects, field users collect data.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
New to terranode? Start with Getting started. Terms like catalog, project, and bundle are defined in the Glossary. Prefer the terminal? See Using the tn CLI.

This is client-facing documentation

Looking for internal architecture, runbooks, or API implementation notes instead? That lives in the separate engineering docs site.

docs.title: Using the tn command line
docs.text:
tn is terranode's command-line client — everything you can do with catalogs, data sources, and uploads through the API, from your terminal or a script, instead of clicking through the app.

Early preview

tn is new and not yet published anywhere you can pip install it from directly — ask your terranode contact for access while that's being set up.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
tn auth login

You'll be asked for your email and password. tn stores a token locally (~/.config/tn/config.json) so you don't have to log in again for every command. If you belong to more than one organization, pick a default:

tn config set-org <organization-id>

(tn orgs list shows the organizations you belong to and their IDs.)

docs.title: Working with catalogs
docs.text:
tn catalogs list
tn catalogs create --name "Field boundaries" --visibility private
tn catalogs get <catalog-id>
tn catalogs update <catalog-id> --name "New name"
tn catalogs delete <catalog-id>

Add --json after tn (e.g. tn --json catalogs list) to get machine-readable output instead of a table — handy for piping into jq or another script.

docs.title: Uploading data into a catalog
docs.text:
tn uploads create <catalog-id> ./roads.geojson --wait

This uploads the file and, with --wait, blocks until terranode has finished turning it into one or more data sources. Drop --wait to return immediately and check later:

tn uploads get <catalog-id> <upload-id>
tn datasources list <catalog-id>

Data sources themselves aren't created or edited directly — they're always the result of an upload finishing processing.

docs.title: Automating without your password
docs.text:
If you want a script, a CI pipeline, or another server to use tn without your personal login, create an API key instead (you need to be an organization owner):

tn orgs api-keys create --name "ci-pipeline" --role editor

This mints a long-lived credential and, by default, switches this machine to use it. If the key is actually meant for somewhere else (a CI secret, a different machine), add --mint-only so your own session here is left alone and the key is just printed for you to copy:

tn orgs api-keys create --name "ci-pipeline" --role editor --mint-only

Wherever the key ends up, set it as TN_TOKEN in that environment:

export TN_TOKEN="<the key you were given>"

List or revoke keys for your organization at any time:

tn orgs api-keys list
tn orgs api-keys revoke <key-id>

See the Glossary for terms like catalog and organization used throughout this page.

docs.title: 1. Join or create your organization
docs.text: The first time you sign in, terranode asks for your organization's details. Every user belongs to exactly one organization — all of your catalogs, projects, and surveys live inside that boundary and are never visible to other organizations.

docs.title: 2. Build (or import) a catalog
docs.text:
Before you can configure a project, you need some GIS layers to work with:

  • Import vector or raster data from disk, or pull it from a cloud bucket you already have (S3, GCS, and similar).
  • Assign a style to each layer so it renders consistently across projects.
  • Tag and describe layers so your team can find them later — see Find anything below.

docs.title: 3. Configure a project
docs.text:
A project ties together:

  • A boundary — the geographic area field work covers.
  • Participating layers from your catalog — the base maps and reference data field users will see on their device.
  • Participating surveys — the forms field users fill out while collecting data. Start from a template when your organization has a reusable base or example form, then customize it for the project.

docs.title: 4. Send your team to the field
docs.text: Field users open the mobile app, sign in, and download the project. The download bundles the boundary, layers, and surveys so the app works with no network connection. As data comes back in, the project dashboard shows submission counts, survey breakdowns, and live tracking.

docs.title: Find anything
docs.text:
The search bar at the top of terranode searches across catalogs, layers, projects, surveys, and users in your organization — one place to find anything, regardless of which "epic" it belongs to.

See the Glossary for definitions of terms used throughout this documentation.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Organization (org) : The tenant boundary in terranode. Every user belongs to exactly one organization. All catalog, project, and survey data is scoped to an organization, both at the application level and, as a defense-in-depth layer, via PostgreSQL Row-Level Security.

terranode (the perennial org) : A built-in, always-present organization owned by the terranode team itself, used to publish a shared base catalog (base maps, reference layers) that other organizations can use without owning.

Catalog : The set of reusable GIS resources — layers, styles, raster and vector sources — that an organization curates. Catalog data is imported and exported, not hand-edited feature-by-feature, in the initial release.

Layer : A single named GIS dataset (vector or raster) in a catalog, with an assigned style and metadata/tags. Layers are owned by exactly one catalog but may be referenced by many projects.

Project : A configured field data collection effort: a boundary, a set of participating catalog layers, and a set of surveys. Projects use catalog data — they never own or duplicate it.

Survey : A configurable form (similar in spirit to SurveyMonkey) that field users fill out on mobile devices while collecting GIS data — points, lines, polygons, and attached media (photos, video, audio). A survey can be created directly or from a survey template.

Survey template : An organization-scoped reusable form definition. Creating a survey from a template copies the template schema into the survey.

System survey template : A global template configured by terranode administrators and listed alongside organization-scoped templates.

Bundle : The offline package a mobile client downloads before a field visit: the project's boundary, participating layers, and survey definitions, packaged so the field app can work with no network connectivity.

Row-Level Security (RLS) : A native PostgreSQL feature enforcing tenant isolation at the database layer, independent of application-level query filtering. Used here as a second, fail-closed layer beneath terranode's org-scoping.
